timeline: You probably assume a modern military can easily stop twenty thousand flightless birds, but the 1932 Emu War proved you wrong.
Western Australian farmers faced a giant crisis.
Twenty thousand starving emus marched straight into their fields.
Desperate settlers begged the government for heavy artillery.
The Minister of Defence readily agreed to send help.
Two soldiers arrived with Lewis machine guns and ten thousand rounds.
But the birds deployed completely unexpected guerrilla tactics.
Army observers noted that each pack seemed to be led by a big black-plumed bird that kept watch.
Machine guns jammed repeatedly in the rough terrain.
Mounting a gun on a truck proved totally useless.
The commander later compared the birds to tanks that could face machine guns with invulnerability.
Public ridicule forced a humiliating military withdrawal.
The flightless birds had completely won the war.
You probably assume a modern military can easily stop twenty thousand flightless birds, but the 1932 Emu War proved you wrong.
